name: Breakdown repair
summary: When a loader, truck or drill breaks down underground, or a crusher, conveyor or pump stops at the mill, the operator radios the maintenance supervisor, who sends a mechanic, millwright or electrician. The tradesperson travels to the equipment, locks it out, finds the fault and repairs it in place, tows it to the shop or waits for parts, then tests it and hands it back. Downtime is set less by the repair itself than by waiting for a free tradesperson, re-entry after blasting, travel down the ramp and parts that must come by road from the nearest towns; the paper work order card is typed into the CMMS a day or more later and failure causes are often lost.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with one ramp-and-shaft underground mine, a 1,000 t/d class mill, about 300 employees on 14-on/14-off rotations living in camp, and a CMMS (ERP maintenance module) fed from paper work order cards.
baseline.notes: Covers owner mobile equipment and mill fixed plant. Hoist breakdowns follow the fixed-plant path. Contractor equipment is repaired by contractors.

trigger: An operator or the mill control room reports by radio that a unit or piece of plant has stopped working.
end_state: The equipment is back in service and the breakdown work order is closed in the CMMS, with a follow-up work request if the fix was temporary.

volume.seasonality: Slightly higher in winter, when cold affects surface equipment, the portal area and the crusher, and after long production pushes that defer PM.

evidence.note: About 32 owner heavy units at 350-450 hours a month (12,000-14,000 machine hours) with a breakdown every 100-150 operating hours, plus 25-40 fixed plant breakdowns; agrees with the organisation file.

surge.cause: extreme cold snap (below about -30 C) affecting surface and portal equipment, ore-handling chutes and the crusher

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a site near Lake Superior in northern Ontario.
Intake, triage, return confirmation and incident reports, about 30 minutes per breakdown plus shift-board work.
er2022 lists 12 owner mine maintenance staff in 2022 against 22 heavy-duty mechanics in the organisation file. FTE estimated from lead hands-on time with a second mechanic on about a third of jobs.
Towing disabled units; stands in for all operators.
Stops, isolation and restarts for about 40 plant breakdowns a month.
About 40 plant breakdowns a month at 3-5 hours each including helpers.
er2022 lists 8 mine electricians; FTE from about 25 electrical faults a month with travel.
Part issues for about 50 breakdowns a month.
Emergency orders for about 12 breakdowns a month.
Card entry and failure coding.

systems.name: Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Incident, inspection and training records system
Mill distributed control system and process historian

resources.name: Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Take the breakdown call
steps.description: The operator of the failed loader, truck, drill or mill equipment calls on the leaky feeder or surface radio. The maintenance supervisor on shift takes the call and writes the unit, location, symptom and time on the shift board.

error.defect_description: The location or symptom is noted wrongly, so the tradesperson brings the wrong tools.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Triage and assign a tradesperson
steps.description: The supervisor decides how urgent the breakdown is (blocking a ramp, stopping the hoist or mill feed, or one of several spare units down) and which trade to send, pulling a mechanic or millwright off planned work if needed.

error.defect_description: The wrong trade is sent and an electrician has to be called later.

next.condition: fixed plant at the mill or crusher

evidence.note: Mobile share follows the fleet and plant in er2022 (about 55 owner mobile units against one mill); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Travel to the unit underground
steps.description: The mechanic finishes or makes safe the job in hand, loads the service truck with tools and common parts and drives down the ramp to the unit, which may be several levels away.

evidence.note: Ramp access in er2022; ballantyne2019 records waiting for fitter as part of breakdown time. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Secure and lock out the unit
steps.description: The mechanic checks the ground and ventilation around the unit, waits for re-entry if the area was just blasted, chocks the wheels, lowers or blocks raised parts and locks and tags the isolation switch before touching the machine.

error.defect_description: Stored hydraulic energy is not released before work.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 107(2), s. 108(2) and s. 185(7)-(8)

evidence.note: Duties stated in the regulation; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Diagnose the fault
steps.description: The mechanic reads the fault codes on the display, checks pressures, leaks and wiring and talks to the operator about what happened, then decides whether to repair in place, tow the unit to the shop, fetch parts or call an electrician.

error.defect_description: The root cause is misread and the wrong part is replaced.

next.condition: repair in place with truck stock

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Repair the unit
steps.description: The mechanic replaces the failed hose, sensor, pump, cylinder seal or other part, tops up fluids and cleans up the spill. Heavier jobs such as a transmission or axle change are done in the shop with a second mechanic.

error.defect_description: The repair is temporary or incomplete and the unit fails again within days.

evidence.note: Breakdowns are recorded against engine, transmission and hydraulics subsystems; repair times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Tow or tram the unit to the shop
steps.description: An operator brings a second loader or the unit itself, if it can move, and tows it up the ramp to the underground shop while the mechanic follows. The ramp is controlled while a disabled unit is moved.

evidence.note: Reg 854 s. 106(2) requires warning to traffic when a vehicle is disabled on a roadway; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Tag the removed component for rebuild
steps.description: The mechanic drains and caps the removed engine, transmission or final drive, fills in the core tag with unit, hours and failure description and has it loaded for the rebuild shop or OEM exchange.

error.defect_description: The failure description is too vague for the rebuilder to find the cause.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Test the unit and hand it back
steps.description: The mechanic removes the locks, starts the unit, checks for leaks and codes, tests the service, emergency and parking brakes, and hands the unit back to the operator by radio.

error.defect_description: A marginal brake passes the test.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105(b) and s. 119.1 (brakes able to stop and hold, each system testable); s. 185(7) on removing locks

evidence.note: Brake duties stated in the regulation; time and failure rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Stop and isolate the circuit
steps.description: The mill shift supervisor has the control room stop the crusher, conveyor or pump line, switch to a standby pump where one exists, and decide whether feed can continue from the fine ore bin while the repair is done.

error.defect_description: Upstream feed is not stopped and a chute or sump overflows.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Travel to the equipment
steps.description: The millwright on shift collects tools and walks or drives to the crusher building, mill floor or pump house. If the millwright is busy on planned work, the job waits until it can be made safe.

evidence.note: The mill sits 16.6 km from the mine portal (er2022), so mill trades are based at the mill; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Lock out the equipment
steps.description: The millwright and the operator apply locks and tags to the motor isolators and valves on the group lockout board, release stored energy in belts, hydraulics and accumulators and test that the equipment cannot start.

error.defect_description: An isolation point is missed on a multi-drive conveyor.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 185(7)-(9) (stop, dissipate stored energy, lock, tag and verify) and s. 158 (locking and tagging programme for electrical work)

evidence.note: Duties stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Diagnose the fault
steps.description: The millwright inspects the failed bearing, belt, chute, pump or gearbox, checks the DCS trend with the control room and decides whether it can be fixed with shop stock, needs parts from the warehouse or is an electrical fault.

error.defect_description: The cause is misread and the part fails again.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Repair the plant equipment
steps.description: The millwright, often with a welder or a second millwright, replaces the bearing, belt, impeller or liner, patches the chute or realigns the drive, and cleans the area for restart.

error.defect_description: Alignment or tension is off and the part fails early.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Diagnose and repair the electrical fault
steps.description: The electrician on shift travels to the unit or plant, locks out the electrical supply under the site locking programme, traces the fault in sensors, harnesses, starters or motors and repairs it. One electrician per shift covers both the mine and the mill.

error.defect_description: An intermittent fault is not found and returns.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 158 (written locking and tagging programme; isolation verified by testing)

evidence.note: er2022 lists 8 mine electricians on rotation; lockout duty from reg854; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Issue parts from the warehouse
steps.description: The tradesperson or supervisor asks the warehouse for the part. The attendant searches the ERP by part number or description, picks it and issues it to the work order; at night the supervisor uses the after-hours key and leaves a note.

error.defect_description: A wrong or superseded part is issued and the repair stops again.

evidence.note: Waiting for parts is a recorded part of breakdown time (ballantyne2019); the stock-out rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Expedite the part from a supplier
steps.description: The buyer phones dealers and OEMs for the part, chooses the fastest source, raises an emergency purchase order and arranges courier or hot-shot delivery to site.

error.defect_description: The part ordered does not fit the unit's serial range.

evidence.note: Buyers work office hours, so a night breakdown waits for the morning; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the part to arrive
steps.description: The supplier ships the part by courier or hot-shot truck from Sudbury, Thunder Bay, Timmins or further, over the highway and the mine access road; the unit or plant stays down or runs on a standby.

error.defect_description: The wrong part arrives.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Restart the plant
steps.description: The mill shift supervisor checks the area is clear, the millwright removes the locks, and the control room restarts the circuit, watching amps, vibration and levels until the equipment runs normally.

error.defect_description: A guard is left off or a tool left in the equipment.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 185(7)-(9) (locks removed only by those who applied them after the machine is clear)

evidence.note: Lock and tag duties in reg854; restart practice and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Confirm return to service
steps.description: The maintenance supervisor confirms with the operator or control room that the equipment is running, updates the shift board and decides whether the event needs an incident report, for example a fire, brake failure or damage.

error.defect_description: A reportable event is treated as an ordinary breakdown.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Write up the work order card
steps.description: At the end of the shift the tradesperson writes the breakdown on a paper work order card: times, symptom, cause, parts used and whether the fix is permanent or temporary.

error.defect_description: Cause and parts are left blank, so failure history is lost.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

steps.name: Report the incident
steps.description: The supervisor enters an incident report in the HSE system with photos and a short description, notifies the safety coordinator and keeps the failed parts for the investigation.

error.defect_description: Key facts or parts are not preserved.

control.basis: Site incident reporting procedure (with notice to the Ministry of Labour where the Occupational Health and Safety Act requires it)

evidence.note: Share of breakdowns that become incidents is the author's estimate; statutory notice duties were not opened, so tier C.

steps.name: Close the work order in the CMMS
steps.description: The planner types the card into the CMMS as a breakdown work order, codes the failure mode and component, posts labour and parts and raises a follow-up work request when the fix was temporary.

error.defect_description: The failure code is guessed from a vague card.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a mid-size Ontario underground mine with a 1,000 t/d class mill.

exceptions.name: Unit towed to the shop
exceptions.description: The unit cannot be repaired where it stopped and is towed up the ramp.

exceptions.name: Part not in stock
exceptions.description: The part is expedited from a supplier and the equipment stays down for one to seven days.

exceptions.name: Electrical fault
exceptions.description: The electrician on shift, shared between mine and mill, is called in.

exceptions.name: Major component replaced
exceptions.description: A failed engine, transmission or final drive is swapped and sent for rebuild.

exceptions.name: Incident report
exceptions.description: A fire, brake failure or damage event is reported in the HSE system.

benchmarks.unit: hours from the radio call to return to service

evidence.note: In-place repairs take a few hours; parts from suppliers add one to several days.
Stated in er2022; breakdowns and planned shutdowns share the remaining 6.7%.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the call to work order closure in the CMMS

evidence.note: Repair within the shift in most cases, then one to three days before the planner enters the card.

pain_points.description: Equipment waits for a free mechanic or electrician, and for re-entry after blasting, before the repair starts.

evidence.note: Waiting for fitter is recorded as part of breakdown time at many underground sites.

pain_points.description: Parts not held on site must come by road, turning a two-hour repair into days of downtime.

evidence.note: Waiting for parts is a recognised component of maintenance stoppages.

pain_points.description: Paper cards with blank causes mean the CMMS failure history cannot guide PM or stocking decisions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for sites re-keying paper cards in 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Breakdowns pull tradespeople off scheduled work, so the weekly schedule slips.

evidence.note: Break-in work is the main threat to weekly schedule compliance.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, effective date December 31, 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Owner underground fleet of 55 units (3 two-boom jumbos, 2 blockholers, 17 LHDs of 2 to 6 yd, 3 30-t trucks, 3 scissor lifts, 4 production drills, 23 light vehicles) plus 17 contractor units (Table 16-9); owner underground labour 111 including 12 mine maintenance and 8 mine electricians, plus 36 contractors (Table 16-10); underground mine scheduled 365 days a year on two 12-hour shifts; ramp access with 30-t trucks and a three-compartment shaft with a double-drum hoist, hoisting at most about 16 hours a day; ore trucked 16.6 km from the portal to the mill; mobile maintenance shop and an asset management and planning office (new in 2021) on site; mill planned at 93.3% availability but 86% in 2021 because of a planned August 2021 shutdown to replace the cone crusher and trash screen, inspect and reinstall the secondary ball mill gearbox with motor alignment and liner inspection, inspect the fine ore bin and repair the coarse ore bin; average throughput 779 t/d.

sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 854: Mines and Mining Plants, under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (consolidated text)
sources.supports: s. 105 (vehicles in safe working condition with brakes that stop and hold under full load); s. 106(4) (operators test service and emergency brakes before using a main ramp); s. 107(2) (wheel chocks whenever a vehicle is maintained or repaired); s. 119.1 (service, emergency and parking brake systems each testable); s. 158 (written locking and tagging programme for electrical work); s. 185(7)-(9) (moving parts stopped, stored energy dissipated, energy isolating devices locked and tagged and verified by testing before work on a machine); s. 82 (hoisting suspended and protection provided when work is done in a shaft compartment); s. 228(2) (drum hoist rope tests at intervals of not more than six months); s. 229(4) (two test trips after rope attachments are reinstalled); s. 248 (daily, weekly, monthly, six-monthly and twelve-monthly examinations of hoisting plant by competent persons, recorded in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book). Read in its current consolidation; the cited duties were in force in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Challenging the Norms: Time Usage Model for Mobile Underground Mining Equipment (white paper)
sources.publisher: RAK Developments (Ray Ballantyne), hosted by AusIMM
sources.supports: Underground mines on 2 x 12-hour shifts record equipment status for all calendar hours; typical maintenance statuses include the 250-hour service and breakdowns by subsystem (engine, transmission, hydraulics); opportunity maintenance when a unit is not required by operations; service overrun beyond the scheduled end; sites record waiting for fitter and waiting for parts within maintenance stoppages; jumbos accumulate diesel hours while travelling and electric hours while drilling.

sources.title: Maintenance Compliance Rate
sources.supports: Weekly schedule compliance (completed scheduled work orders over scheduled work orders) of 80-90% in disciplined programmes; break-in work after the schedule freeze kept to 10-15% of weekly hours; freeze 70-80% of available hours with a joint operations-maintenance review; a site at 65% compliance can gain 15-20 points from a one-week freeze and a joint scheduling meeting; backlog ageing buckets 0-7, 8-14, 15-30 and 31+ days.

assumptions: touch_min records the lead tradesperson's minutes; about a third of jobs use a second person, which is included in the role FTE.
The simulator does not remember which path a case took, so the parts and electrical steps send cases back to the mobile and plant repair steps in the 72:28 proportion of breakdowns.

Equipment held is recorded against the LHD pool for mobile breakdowns (about half of the heavy fleet) and against the crusher for plant breakdowns; the occupied minutes include waiting for the tradesperson.
Hoist breakdowns are rare and follow the fixed-plant path; the hoist is not listed separately.
Repaired plant goes back to mill-crushing or mill-grind-leach; the organisation file lists repaired_equipment only to mine-shift-control, so a link to mill-grind-leach is added here.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's.
